title: Origins — 1885–1930
description: The earliest sports cars were lightweight experiments: bespoke coachwork, hand-built engines and a focus on agility. This era introduced design languages that would inform later icons.
credit: Lars-Göran Lindgren / CC BY-SA 4.0 (via Wikimedia Commons)
author: Lars-Göran Lindgren
curatorNotes: Provenance: early competition and coachbuilt examples. Display on a low plinth with a visible chassis cutaway panel to reveal construction methods.

technicalSpecs.notes: Emphasis on lightness, narrow-track geometry, and coachbuilt bodies.

educationalValue: Explains early powertrain design, coachbuilding, and the experimental nature of early automotive engineering.
emotionalEngagement: Evokes craft, rarity, and human-scale engineering; visitors connect with hand-made detail.
presentation: Label with provenance, maker notes, and an interactive timeline showing manufacturing techniques.

title: Golden Era — 1950s–1970s
description: Styling matured into identity. Manufacturers like Ferrari, Aston Martin, and Porsche turned performance into emotional storytelling through proportion, color, and sound.
author: Vauxford
curatorNotes: Highlight design proportion, coachline, and the role of sound in emotional design. Include a short audio clip of the engine note.

technicalSpecs.notes: Styling becomes identity; coachwork and proportion are key teaching points.

educationalValue: Explores design language and the relationship between form and emotion in automotive design.
emotionalEngagement: Strong — colour, proportion and sound create an immediate emotional response.
presentation: Place with curated lighting, period photography, and designer quotes.

title: Supercars — 1980s–2000s
description: Aerodynamics, composite materials, and turbocharged performance created visceral machines. This era elevated cars to cultural icons and racing technology trickled down to road cars.
author: Palauenc05
curatorNotes: Show cross-sections of aerodynamic elements and composite panel samples; explain how racing tech influenced road cars.

technicalSpecs.notes: Rapid advances in materials and aerodynamics; styling becomes extreme and iconic.

educationalValue: Demonstrates materials science, aerodynamic design, and the intersection of performance and spectacle.
emotionalEngagement: High — these are showpieces that often define popular culture imagery.
presentation: Use low, angled plinths and mirrored floor panels to emphasize silhouette.

title: Modern Performance — 2000s–2010s
description: Electronics, stability control, and advanced engineering refined driver experience, offering both blistering speed and precision handling.
credit: Matti Blume / CC BY-SA 4.0 (via Wikimedia Commons)
author: Matti Blume
curatorNotes: Focus on electronics, chassis systems, and how driver aids changed the capability envelope. Include an interactive demo of traction-control effects.

technicalSpecs.platform: Multi-link suspensions, advanced traction and stability control
technicalSpecs.notes: Systems integration and software became as important as mechanical design.

educationalValue: Teaches systems engineering and how electronics altered vehicle behaviour and safety.
emotionalEngagement: Balanced — sophisticated performance with driver-focused interfaces.
presentation: Interactive kiosks show telemetry and driver data; comparison displays of analogue vs digital gauges.

title: Electrification & Hybrids — 2010s–Today
description: Hybrid and electric platforms redefined performance parameters: instant torque, battery packaging, and new approaches to weight distribution and cooling.
author: Alexander-93
curatorNotes: Explain battery chemistry, packaging trade-offs, and regenerative systems. Use interactive visualisations of energy flow under acceleration and braking.

technicalSpecs.notes: Discuss charging infrastructure, range, and the new design constraints of EV packaging.

educationalValue: Explains fundamentals of electrification, trade-offs, and environmental considerations.
emotionalEngagement: Emerging — mixes heritage cues with futuristic performance; surprises visitors with instant torque demos.
presentation: Transparent cutaways of battery modules, and touchscreens explaining thermal management.

title: The Now — Autonomy & Connectivity
description: Today performance intersects with autonomy, connectivity, and sustainability. Designers balance heritage cues with new, data-driven experiences.
author: MrWalkr
curatorNotes: Discuss autonomy, software-defined vehicles, and sustainable manufacturing. Contrast heritage brands with new entrants.

technicalSpecs.powertrain: High-power electric architectures and software stacks
technicalSpecs.notes: Performance is now measured by software, connectivity and user experience as much as raw metrics.

educationalValue: Invites debate on future mobility, ethics of autonomy, and the cultural role of the sports car.
emotionalEngagement: Futuristic awe, curiosity and debate about what ‘performance’ will mean.
presentation: Mixed-media installations combining physical artifacts with digital storylines and live telemetry.
